title: Compact model adoption friction ledger and actionable integration runbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: engineering and GTM teams are increasingly asked to evaluate compact (<=7B) model families for latency-and-cost-sensitive customers, but we lack a single, actionable ledger that consolidates friction factors (quantization compatibility, kernel/driver constraints, licensing, accuracy delta on Redwood evals, toolchain maturity) and direct integration recipes. Goal: create a persistent 'friction ledger' + runbook that the product team, solutions engineering, and runtime engineering can use to (a) quickly estimate integration effort, (b) recommend migration thresholds and fallbacks, and (c) surface procurement/contract flags for enterprise sales. Deliverables: 1) CSV/Sheet catalog of 30 candidate compact models with scored friction axes; 2) 1-page integration recipe per high-priority model (kernel/quantization notes, recommended runtime config, expected throughput/latency delta vs baseline), 3) decision thresholds for recommending Dedicated vs Hosted offering, 4) checklist for legal/KMS/licensing review, 5) README for Solutions Engineers with templated PR and customer demo script. Acceptance criteria: ledger covers top-30 market-relevant compact variants, each model has a minimum-data integration recipe, two sample internal pilot integrations completed (one Hosted, one Dedicated), and the playbook is reviewed by Eng + Legal + Solutions. Business impact: reduce exploratory integration time from ~6 weeks to ~2 weeks and accelerate competitive responses when customers demand low-latency/low-cost substitutes.
